ok.de: „Rarely“ am Satzanfang verlangt die Umstellung wie in einer Frage: Rarely have we seen.
ok.en: “Rarely” at the start requires inversion as in a question: Rarely have we seen.

wrong.de: Das Hilfsverb steht vor dem Subjekt: Rarely have we seen.
wrong.en: The auxiliary comes before the subject: Rarely have we seen.

wrong.de: Mit seen bleibt es bei have, nicht did: Rarely have we seen.
wrong.en: With seen keep have, not did: Rarely have we seen.

ok.de: Nach „Only after“ steht did vor dem Subjekt, das Verb in der Grundform: did we approve.
ok.en: After “Only after”, did stands before the subject and the verb takes the base form: did we approve.

wrong.de: Vor das Subjekt we gehört did: Only after the pilot did we approve.
wrong.en: Before the subject we you need did: Only after the pilot did we approve.

wrong.de: Nach did steht die Grundform: approve, nicht approved.
wrong.en: After did comes the base form: approve, not approved.

ok.de: Zu „no sooner“ gehört than: No sooner had we signed than the prices rose.
ok.en: “No sooner” goes with than: No sooner had we signed than the prices rose.

wrong.de: When gehört zu hardly. Zu no sooner gehört than.
wrong.en: When goes with hardly. No sooner goes with than.

ok.de: Nach Should you steht die Grundform ohne will: Should you need help.
ok.en: After Should you the base form follows without will: Should you need help.

wrong.de: Nach Should you steht kein will, nur die Grundform.
wrong.en: After Should you there is no will, only the base form.

wrong.de: Die förmliche Bedingung beginnt mit Should you.
wrong.en: The formal condition starts with Should you.
